title: Reflective performance sprintbook — Derek Liu
content:
Purpose: capture sprint-by-sprint evidence, micro-experiments, and short manager-facing narratives I can drop into 1:1s, calibration, and promo prep. This is intentionally messy — meant as a working brain dump and checklist.

Snapshot (Mar 05, 2026):
- Role: Senior People Ops (IC, cross-functional project lead)
- Current priorities: reduce early ramp time for new hires; close loop on 'manager enablement' playbook; pilot a lightweight performance calibration snack for Eng L2-L4.
- Signal targets for next 12 weeks: new hire time-to-contributor down from 8 -> 6 weeks (measured by first customer-impact PR / first autonomous hire onboarding task), manager NPS for onboarding >= 85, 3 managers onboarded to playbook, 1 documented failure mode + fix.

Quick metric signals (evidence to cite):
- New hire onboarding survey (n=12, last 90d): avg satisfaction 4.1/5 (+0.4 from previous cohort). Note: small n, skew toward Eng interns.
- Time-to-first-meaningful-production: rolling median 55 days (target 42). Biggest delta in infra & SRE hires.
- Manager playbook adoption: 2 live cohorts (pilot), 9 unique managers used the checklist.
- Calibration pilot: 6 teams in pilot. Outcome: one major divergence flagged between manager-reported vs. peer feedback; we created a quick remediation checklist.

Recent wins to call out (short, concrete):
- Launched onboarding 'first-30' template for Eng new hires (saved ~3h/week for on-call mentor rotations). Anecdote: Ash said the template cut their ramp meeting prep by half.
- Closed loop on offer-to-accept process: reduced offer cushion extension requests by 20% by clarifying comp timeline.
- Ran two manager enablement sessions; one manager reported measurable improvement in direct report 1:1 quality the following week.

Tricky feedback / backlog items (honest):
- Perceived: I move on to the next thing too fast. Evidence: two incomplete follow-ups in last 6 weeks (JIRA-OPS-4804, -4816). Fix: add explicit "follow-up owner" and calendar reach-outs.
- Measuring impact: need to instrument 'ramp' definition consistently across teams — current metric noisy. Action: partner with data (Lina) to agree on canonical signal.

Concrete examples (stories to use in 1:1s / calibrations):
- Story A: New hire E found onboarding doc inconsistent across infra teams, needed 10x shadowing. I pulled owners, created a condensed checklist, then paired with infra lead to run a focused 2-hr sync. Result: E completed first autonomous infra task in 18 days after the sync.
- Story B: Manager M improved 1:1 preparation after my session; report directly told me they felt heard and shifted goal cadence. Use this to show coaching impact.

Manager prep script (bullet prompts I can read or paste):
- Opening one-liner: "Quick status: pilot onboarding is showing early lift (satisfaction +0.4) but time-to-contributor still behind target; I prioritized measurement and a targeted infra play to close the delta."
- Two things I'm proud of: launch of 'first-30' template (reduced mentor prep), and successful manager enablement session that led to behavior change.
- Two things I need help with: unblock on data alignment for ramp metric (need a 2-hr working session with data team); support to escalate incomplete cross-team docs (ask: OK to message Eng PM triage channel?).
- Ask for career development: more opportunities to lead cross-org operational initiatives (1 new program per quarter); request to be considered for shadowing during calibration cycle (exposure to exec-level synthesis).

Open asks (prioritized):
1) Data alignment meeting (2 hrs) — owner: Derek + Lina + analytics (JIRA-OPS-4821).
2) OK to send short escalation note to Eng PM triage to prioritize missing onboarding artifacts (ask for manager sign-off).
3) Sponsor intro to senior people partner in Platform to co-lead a cross-functional onboarding charter.

Micro-experiments (2-week cycles):
- Experiment 1 (Wk1-2): 'Day-0 buddy check' — send a templated Slack DM to buddy and new hire on day 0 to confirm first-week schedule and blockers. Measure: buddy response time, new hire first-week survey (NPS).
- Experiment 2 (Wk3-4): 'Focused infra 2-hr sync' for hires flagged as >60d ramp. Measure reduction in time-to-first-autonomous-task.
- Experiment 3 (continuous): 'Manager 1:1 checklist' nudges — in pilot cohort, reminder DM 24h before 1:1 with 3 suggested prompts. Measure: self-reported 1:1 usefulness.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: pilot results not statistically meaningful. Mitigation: increase sample size by adding two more teams next cycle; focus on qualitative signals when n small.
- Risk: manager bandwidth to adopt playbook low. Mitigation: shorter artifact (1-pager) + office hour drop-ins + manager champion in each org.

Career signal mapping (how I want to demonstrate growth):
- Project scope: ownership of cross-org onboarding charter (shows program leadership).
- Influence: evidence of behavior change (manager feedback, direct report surveys) and documented process that scales.
- Craft: improve measurement & storytelling — deliver one short org-level synthesis for Q2 retros.

Quick evidence log (one-liners I can paste):
- "Reduced onboarding mentor prep time by ~50% via the first-30 template; mentor feedback collected 2/26."
- "Pilot manager enablement cohort: 9 managers; 67% reported immediate change in 1:1 structure (post-session survey)."
- "Calibration pilot surfaced one major divergence that we remediated with a documented checklist; saved an escalated review."

To-do (next 14 days):
- [ ] Book 2-hr data alignment working session with Lina and Analytics (target week of Mar 8).
- [ ] Draft short escalation note for Eng PM triage and share with manager for sign-off.
- [ ] Run micro-experiment 1 with cohort starting Mar 9; capture baseline.
- [ ] Write 1-page 'manager playbook: 3 quick moves' and share to pilot managers.

Notes-to-self / reminders (informal):
- When asked about "impact": lead with behavior change example (manager 1:1) + a measured signal (survey NPS or time-to-contributor).
- Keep stories short (30–60s) — name, problem, action, result.
- If pressed on numbers, be transparent about cohort size and next steps to scale measurement.

Last quick reflection (prompt for next sprint):
- What small replication test can I run that proves whether the playbook is actually used (not just downloaded)? Idea: require a 1-line sync note from manager after 3rd 1:1 post-playbook — use that as adoption signal.

End of sprintbook dump. Revisit after data session and after next manager check-in.
